value.body: The Australian Medical Council (AMC) assesses doctors trained outside Australia. On the Standard pathway, an Indian MBBS graduate passes the AMC computer-adaptive MCQ exam and then either the AMC Clinical Examination or a workplace-based assessment, followed by supervised practice, to reach general registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

items.label: Written exam
items.note: Computer-adaptive; must be passed before applying for registration

items.label: Clinical step
items.note: Workplace-based assessment places are limited and need registration first

items.label: Supervised practice
items.source: Medical Board of Australia, Standard pathway

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A primary medical degree from a school listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools, a completed internship, primary-source verification of documents through the AMC (via ECFMG's EPIC), and meeting the Board's English language standard. Then the CAT MCQ, the clinical exam or WBA, and a supervised position approved by the Board.

value.title: At a glance
items: The process usually takes years and involves significant exam, verification and visa costs.
Finding a first supervised job in Australia is often the hardest step.
Doctors with UK, US, Canadian, Irish or New Zealand qualifications/experience may use the separate Competent Authority pathway; specialists have their own pathways.
